candidateSchema: India-oriented Phone Series Design Judgment 0.5.0 Candidate
question: Can one nested series-level Schema produce four visibly related members while keeping camera hierarchy, rigid-material junctions, and Paisley/Boteh expression coherent?

visibleEvidence: exactly two real lenses and one subordinate tail flash share one horizontal axis
the rigid camera bridge has a clean single attachment boundary
graphite phone separates clearly from the warm ivory background
outputs.candidateFinding: camera order and material continuity work, but the right end remains capsule-rounded rather than visibly tapered, so the Boteh family contour is weak

visibleEvidence: three descending lenses and one smaller flash are coaxial and legible
camera segmentation and hard rear surface meet through a precise boundary
directional rear grooves carry the cultural relationship without crossing hardware
outputs.candidateFinding: the family grammar is clear, though the rear grooves are stronger and larger than the requested low-contrast microtexture

visibleEvidence: the enlarged main camera, two smaller lenses, and tail flash retain one strict axis
the rigid tapered enclosure gives the clearest rounded-body-to-tail Boteh relationship
the silver body and dark aubergine background separate strongly
outputs.candidateFinding: best compliance with both family camera grammar and restrained transparent-layer cultural expression

visibleEvidence: Standard hardware is preserved as three lenses and one smaller coaxial flash
all camera and rear parts read as rigid with clear seams
one non-repeating engraved Paisley field remains separate from camera hardware and contrasts against a pale cool background
outputs.candidateFinding: the cultural intensity ladder is visible, but the camera enclosure again resolves as a rounded capsule and the engraving becomes more literal and ornate than the intended abstract micro-engraved field

candidateVerdict: reject for promotion; revise the candidate as one coherent topology-neutral model
provisionalLearning: The candidate improves lens/flash hierarchy, hard-material continuity, and background separation, but gives Paisley too much authority over the primary camera silhouette. Preserve functional camera topology first, then carry culture through internal functional or structural order rather than a rear skin. Do not hardcode the liked elongated rectangle as a universal Transsion family shape.
userFeedback: Concepts 1 and 2 are acceptable. Concept 2 handles the camera zone especially well as one integrated elongated rectangular expression. Concept 3 does not reveal its cultural texture. Concepts 3 and 4 have unattractive, hesitant triangular camera-zone forms. Cultural expression should integrate modestly with functional or structural parts instead of sitting separately as a skin, while remaining restrained. Follow-up: the elongated rectangle is one valid Transsion approach, not a Schema invariant; the next model must support multiple coherent camera topologies.
